headline_findings: P08-007 (medium): the row's load-bearing premise that one second-masculine-singular addressee governs MT 35:1-35:15 is false at MT 35:9 (2mp verb of knowing) and MT 35:13 (three 2mp forms, no singular form); that premise is what the row uses to decline the internal splits at 35:4/35:5 and 35:9/35:10. Boundary kept: petuchah on both seams, one strict-form onset, single interior setumah after MT 35:13 coinciding with neither proposed split.

P08-010 (support): every Hebrew and mark fact holds, including the exposed count — MT 36:2-36:7 carries six messenger formulas, one per verse, with no refrain between any two. A seven-count for the same stretch is accounted for by the extra summons to hear at MT 36:4, a different device.

P08-011 (low): the blanket claim that all four K/Q pairs at MT 36:13-36:14 are rendered with morpheme separators stripped is untrue for two of the four — the first note on MT 36:13 and the second on MT 36:14 carry no separator in the witness. No fabricated composite: all seven written/read forms in the row reconstruct their witness note entries codepoint-for-codepoint once the separator is removed.

P08-012 (medium): at MT 36:16 the row calls its onset 'the fourth and last' hard seam since MT 33:1 and enumerates 33:1/33:23/34:1; the same byte-identical form also stands at MT 35:1, making 36:16 the fifth, and it is not the last (MT 37:15, MT 38:1 follow). Separately its WEB quotation at MT 36:22 is not verbatim (straight apostrophe for the translation's right single quotation mark). Onset itself is the strongest class available, so the decision is keep.

P08-013 (medium, confidence moves to medium): the 'for' sub-onset the row places at MT 36:24 is not in the MT — the verse opens waw + first-person perfect with no causal particle; 'For' is the translation's supplied conjunction and the translation also prints a paragraph there. No paragraph mark stands after MT 36:23; the nearest marks fall after MT 36:21 and MT 36:32, so the witness's closed section runs MT 36:22-36:32 and this row's onset lies inside it. Close side (MT 36:32 utterance + setumah, MT 36:33 messenger re-onset) is firm, hence a grade move rather than a span change.

P08-014 (low): MT 36:36 carries a 3mp recognition clause naming the nations before its emphatic closing clause — the same construction disclosed at MT 36:23 — and the row names only the emphatic clause, so the internal close it grades as non-final actually stacks recognition + emphatic + setumah, the same combination it treats as row-final at MT 36:38. Non-finality is nonetheless correctly grounded in the messenger re-onset at MT 36:37, so the span is kept.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Routed read-form question: instances recorded, not adjudicated. Seven read forms are rendered across this cluster (MT 35:9, MT 35:12, two at MT 36:13, two at MT 36:14, one at MT 36:15). None occurs in the running-text extract, which carries the written forms; each reconstructs its witness note entry exactly once the morpheme separator is removed; 3 of the 7 entries carry a separator and 4 carry none. I reproduce none of the seven and name the sites instead.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the two sub-cases are not one question — a separator removed from an entry that has one is a rendering choice, while an entry that never had one cannot have been stripped, which is the narrower point the MT 35:9/35:12/36:13/36:14 findings rest on. The toolkit's own tier description, which accepts a read form from the note layer when a K/Q keyword stands within 160 characters and compares against the note's raw split bytes, is the nearest sanctioning language I found.
